t: Amounts appropriated by this Act to the Department of the Interior shall be available for obligation and expenditure not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This provision only sets a timing rule for when appropriated funds become available to the Department of the Interior. There is no tempting reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: Amounts appropriated by this Act to the Department of the Interior shall be available for obligation and expenditure not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This provision only sets a deadline for when funds appropriated to the Department of the Interior can be spent. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision. Seeing it as procedural because of the timing requirement is wrong, because no outsider takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that limits the time frame for spending federal funds. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The text describes internal fiscal management rather than public participation.
qwen_chat.s: Amounts appropriated by this Act to the Department of the Interior shall be available for obligation and expenditure not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for the Department of the Interior, which interacts with the public, this implies participation. However, the text itself is purely a fiscal limitation on the availability of appropriated funds. It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or interaction with non-federal entities. It is a standard appropriations clause.
